description: Agent Triage: submit a stated severity scale with each queue item’s severity and urgency assessment: each level of the scale (critical, high, medium or low) with the criteria an item meets at that level; and each item with its id, what it is about, the severity assessed, the stated criterion the assessment cites, the assessment note as written, read for gut-feel wording such as feels urgent, I think or probably, the urgency assessed on the same scale and its basis, such as a deadline, an outage window or a time limit. The signed report gives the scale, every item with its rating, the level whose criterion it cites, any gut-feel wording and its status as assessed, partly_assessed, guessed, off_scale, mismatched, unassessed or unconfirmed, counts the items rated, assessed, guessed and unassessed, and lists every gut-feel word found, and names severity guessed rather than assessed: ratings at a level the scale does not define, ratings by feel with no stated criterion and ratings that cite another level’s criterion; then items left unrated, ratings with no criterion or one the scale does not state, and urgency missing or stated with no basis, with the fix for each. This reads queue items rated against a stated scale: the severity of failure conditions in alert rules is wever_observability-alert-check, and the severity levels an incident response plan defines are wever_incident-plan-check. Verdict severity_guessed, severity_uneven, severity_unassessed or severity_assessed. POST /api/triage-severity-check. Reads only the recorded queue items and records in the call: no network request, fetch, money movement, message, sharing, configuration change or external write; no item is captured, ranked, routed, escalated or closed and no queue is changed. Agent Triage reads how an agent sorts incoming work, from the item captured at intake to the disposition it ends with: it is not multi-agent coordination (how a group of agents organizes shared work, with its own escalation path, the wever_coordination checks; triage escalation is a single queue item breaching its threshold and moving up a tier, with its context attached), not the promises an agent has made (promises and deadlines once they are made, the wever_commitment checks; triage decides handling order and routing before any promise exists), not delegation (handing work off with authority, the wever_delegation checks; triage assigns incoming items to queues and owners, a sorting decision rather than a delegation) and not the dates inside one document (wever_deadline-check; the triage checks read a queue of items over time). Paid URL: 0.10 USDC per call on Base via x402 exact, with the shared 10 signed-wallet free calls per rolling 30 days. Bind X-Wever-Wallet-Proof to the exact JSON arguments and the tool route. Returns a report with an Ed25519 signed receipt. Contract: /api/agent-triage-contract. Human page: https://weverlabs.com/agent-triage/.

items.description: Each queue item with its severity and urgency assessment.

criterion.description: The stated criterion the assessment cites.

id.description: The item id, such as q1.

rationale.description: The assessment note as written, read for gut-feel wording such as feels urgent or I think.

severity.description: The severity assessed: critical, high, medium or low.

urgency.description: How soon it needs handling, on the same scale.

urgency_basis.description: Why it is that urgent: a deadline, an outage window or a time limit, as stated.

label.description: Optional name recorded in the report.

scale.description: The stated severity scale, one entry per level.

criteria.description: The stated criteria an item meets at this level, such as checkout down for every customer.

level.description: The severity level: critical, high, medium or low.

name: wever_triage-severity-check
title: Triage severity check
